anatomy.intro: Green and variegated sectors share the same notched, ribbed stem.

parts.function: A notch beneath an areole gives the rib its characteristic chin-shaped projection.
parts.label: Chin-like rib

parts.function: This cushion bears the short, curved spine cluster.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Green tissue contains chlorophyll used to capture light for photosynthesis.
parts.label: Green sector

parts.function: Lighter yellow and pink sectors interrupt the green pattern across the stem.
parts.label: Variegated sector

flowers.text: Costa Farms describes creamy to pinkish flowers for this variegated selection. The species produces fleshy fruits that ripen from gray-green to red and contain small black seeds.

growth.note: The notches beneath the areoles give each rib a row of small chin-like projections, the feature behind the common name chin cactus.

stages.text: A compact stem already displays rib notches and patches of color.
stages.title: Small globe

stages.text: Growth enlarges the globe; the exact distribution of colored sectors varies.
stages.title: Wider body

stages.text: A mature stem may produce flowers or offsets while retaining a compact habit.
stages.title: Established plant

habitat.text: The wild species grows in rocky places in Paraguay and northeastern Argentina. This cultivated variegated form combines green tissue with yellow and pink sectors and grows on its own roots.

image.alt: Own-root variegated moon cactus with numbered chin-shaped rib, areole, green sector and yellow-pink variegated sector.

lookalikes.name: Grafted neon moon cactus
lookalikes.text: A graft has a colored scion visibly joined to a separate green rootstock. This collection plant retains green tissue in its own body and is recorded on its own roots.

mature.text: Costa Farms gives about 15 cm tall or wide for its variegated selection, with a compact rounded body.

milestones.text: Joined the collection from Costa Farms.
milestones.title: Acquired

nameStory.text: Gymnocalycium means naked calyx: its flower buds lack the spines and hairs found on many other cactus flower tubes. The name refers to flowers, not a completely spineless body.
